digest.component_or_area: op-cert service signing and key management
propositions: Op-cert signing must load key material exactly once at process startup from a single validated source (REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY) before queue/worker/network/workspace creation, rejecting missing, conflicting, unreadable, non-regular, malformed, encrypted, or non-Ed25519 inputs.

The startup-bound signing key must be copied to a process-owned 0700 directory with 0600 file permissions, remain stable for process lifetime, observe replacement only after restart, and be cleaned up without modifying the deployment source.

Both out-of-opcert_service producer chains (completion via transition_close.sign_completion_verdict and plan-review via attest/generation.sign_manifest) must accept and thread an optional context-local OpcertSigner binding through mint_opcert_record and _sign_manifest_under_lock, signing from the injected binding when supplied by the service and falling back to environment resolution for developer-local callers.
Concurrent and timed-out jobs must maintain context-local isolation of signer, principal, and push policy state with one immutable startup signer and no workspace push remote.

The op-cert application runtime must have zero runtime dependency on SSM, boto3, AWS region configuration, or per-job key retrieval; the key must be materialized outside the container by fetch-secrets.sh and bind-mounted read-only with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH.

Secret and key material must never appear in process repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, child processes, or persisted envelopes beyond the existing public signature.
